decision: Reject the empirical Gate-I claim of jointly identifying raw-language equivalence and latent intervention partitions under the current public-benchmark constraint. Retain RQ-001-T1 only as a not-yet-adopted theory candidate about when language strictly refines trajectory-identifiable causal equivalence classes.
new_primary_sources: Gkountouras et al. ICLR 2025 Language Agents Meet Causality
Richens et al. ICML 2025 General agents need world models

benchmark_audit.CausalPhys: ineligible: curated image/video QA with expert typed DAGs, no unknown-target interactive trajectory identification; external judge LLM
benchmark_audit.SILG_RTFM: ineligible for Gate I: no independent intervention family or causal abstraction ground truth
benchmark_audit.J_CRe3: ineligible: reference grounding without mechanism interventions
benchmark_audit.CausalTriplet: ineligible: intervention structure without episode-aligned free language

identifiability_condition: A necessary but insufficient condition is I(M;L|X)>0, where X includes state, action, history, reward, time, policy phase and environment identity. A qualified benchmark must exhibit competing partitions equivalent under X, separated by correct L, destroyed by matched language shuffle, and preserved by semantic paraphrase.
